question: Is the parastatal mandated to prepare its spatial and/or sectoral plans in coordination with the ULG(s) within its jurisdiction?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. No provision in the Citation Sheet requires BWSSB to prepare its spatial or sectoral plans in coordination with, or with approval from, the GBA or the City Corporations. The only nearby mechanisms are advisory or run in the opposite direction. | EVIDENCE: (1) BWSSB Act 1964 s.14 (FAOLEX copy, as amended). The State Government 'shall constitute a Consultative Committee'. Its members are Board members plus 3-9 others appointed 'after consultation with' bodies representing the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bangalore, the Bangalore City Improvement Trust Board and water consumers. Its function is 'to advise the Board on major questions of policy and major schemes'. This is an advisory body, and ULG input only shapes who is appointed. It is not mandatory ULG consultation on plan preparation. The Act names the old Corporation, and no official source in the sheet shows the GBA substituted. (2) BWSSB Act s.36 and s.38 cover water supply to the Corporation and public hydrants. They do not deal with plan preparation. (3) Greater Bengaluru Governance Act 2024 (Gazette text as published 24.04.2025), s.14(2)(a): the GBA 'shall be the Planning Authority' under the Karnataka T&CP Act 1961 for the Greater Bengaluru Area. Section 15(5) says the GBA 'may assign the task of planning the major infrastructural projects' to public authorities and that 'The agencies shall be bound to assist the Greater Bengaluru Authority when called up on to do so.' This is a GBA-to-
quote: to advise the Board on major questions of policy and major schemes;

The only BWSSB Act text in the sheet is a FAOLEX copy, which is a blocked mirror and only a lead. No BWSSB Rules or Regulations are in the sheet, and the Governance Act and T&CP Act were only partly read. (3) The evidence found does not fit a band above 0. Section 14 sets up a State-constituted Consultative Committee that advises the Board on major policy and schemes. The Municipal Corporation of the City of Bangalore and the BCITB are only bodies consulted on who is appointed. That is not mandatory ULG consultation on plan preparation. Section 15(2) makes BWSSB prepare schemes, and schemes costing over a crore need State Government approval, not ULG approval. In the Governance Act, s.15(5) lets the GBA assign infrastructure planning to agencies, which is discretionary and runs from the GBA to the agency. The sheet does not show the GBA substituted for the Corporation named in s.14. A person should confirm the scale and obtain an official copy of the Act. If every layer is confirmed to lack any ULG coordination duty, the score would be 0. If the s.14 committee were treated as formal consultation, the most that could be supported is the 'may' band (2.5 of 10, so 1.25 of 5). That reading is unlikely.

The nearest band is 0 (no formal role), but a 0 needs affirmative absence, which I could not establish. BDA Act s.30(3) refers Authority-Corporation disputes on street and open-space transfer to Government. BDA Act s.67 inserted s.81-B in the T&CP Act, making BDA the local Planning Authority for the Bangalore local planning area. question: Is the parastatal mandated to prepare its spatial and/or sectoral plans in coordination with the ULG(s) within its jurisdiction?
step2_answer: ANSWER: No provision in the Citation Sheet requires BMRDA to prepare its structure plan or other plans in coordination with the ULG (the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and its City Corporations). I found no ULG approval, concurrence, joint preparation or mandatory consultation. Absence is not affirmed, because the full T&CP Act text and the Rules were not read. The bands are on a 0-10 scale but Max Score is 5 (SCALE-MISMATCH), so no score is proposed. | EVIDENCE: BMRDA Act 1985 s.9(1)(ii): the Authority's function is 'to prepare a structure plan for the development of the Bangalore Metropolitan Region'. The section has no consultation or ULG-approval requirement. s.9(1)(ix) is a function 'to co-ordinate the activities of the Bangalore Development Authority, the Corporation of the City of Bangalore, ...'. That is BMRDA coordinating other bodies' activities, not a duty to plan with the ULG. s.10 requires other authorities to get BMRDA permission for specified developments, which runs from the ULG to BMRDA. The Act's text is on an unofficial host (India Water Portal). T&CP Act s.81-C (inserted by the BMRDA Act s.31): Planning Authorities in the region submit their plans to the State Government 'through' BMRDA for approval, and BMRDA exercises the Director of Town Planning's powers. That is BMRDA reviewing others' plans, not a ULG role in BMRDA's plans. The GBA Act 2024 s.(2)(a) makes GBA the 'Planning Authority' under the T&CP Act for the Greater Bengaluru Area. It also provi
quote: (ii) to prepare a structure plan for the development of the Bangalore Metropolitan Region;
provision: s.9(1)(ii), s.9(1)(ix), s.31 (inserting T&CP Act s.81-C)
comments: I left the score blank. The BMRDA Act text I read has no provision that requires BMRDA to prepare its structure plan in coordination with, or with the approval of, the ULG. Section 9(1)(ii) gives BMRDA the function of preparing the structure plan, and it has no consultation clause. Section 9(1)(ix) makes BMRDA coordinate the activities of other bodies. Section 10 and the T&CP Act s.81-C (inserted by s.31) run the other way, because ULGs and Planning Authorities have to go through BMRDA. A 0 band needs affirmative absence. I did not read the full T&CP Act (BMRDA-11), the GBA Act (BMRDA-10) or the BMRDA Rules and Regulations, so I cannot confirm that absence. I also did not check whether the Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee or the 2025 Bill (BMRDA-12) creates a consultation duty. The BMRDA Act s.3(3)(d) names the 'Mayor, Corporation of the City of Bangalore' as a board member. That is representation, not a mandate to plan in coordination, and no successor substitution by the GBA was verified. If affirmative absence were confirmed, the band would be 0, which scores 0. If the T&CP Act or the Rules require mandatory consultation, the band would be 5 or 7.5 on the 0-10 scale, which scores 2.5 or 3.75 of 5. A person should confirm both points.
